title: Regenerate new, cycling human scalp follicles for androgenetic alopecia

concept.text: Create an expandable supply of new functional follicles, rather than redistribute existing follicles or reactivate miniaturized ones. Human hair-bearing skin organoids and murine follicle-regeneration results establish preclinical milestones, not clinical completion. Proposed completion test: Regulatory authorization following controlled human evidence that newly generated follicles produce cosmetically useful terminal scalp hair, with a prespecified density improvement sustained for at least 24 months and evidence of repeat cycling, plus acceptable long-term safety. Test set by: Proposed editorial test; FDA, PMDA or another stringent regulator would decide authorization. No accepted clinical density-and-durability standard for follicle cloning was identified. Overlaps: DER-01. Sources given: [Primary human hair-bearing skin organoid study](https://scholarworks.indianapolis.iu.edu/server/api/core/bitstreams/69fe8f63-4ef7-4a2b-b4b6-e2609a8d5d84/content) ; [OrganTech February 2026 follicle-regeneration research announcement](https://www.organ-tech.jp/en/topics/pdf/2026/Hair_Regeneration_OrganTech_Inc%2CFeb_20_2026.pdf).

page.title: De novo human hair follicle regeneration for androgenetic alopecia
page.definition: An expandable cell source produces new human scalp follicles that grow terminal hair—the thick, long hair of the adult scalp—and repeat growth, regression and rest after transplantation into people with androgenetic alopecia, or pattern hair loss.

goal.need: Among 1,390 Australian men, pattern hair loss involving the crown affected 31% of those aged 40–55 and 53% of those aged 65–69. Medicines can slow loss or stimulate existing hairs. Transplants move follicles from elsewhere on the scalp, leaving people with sparse donor hair, including some with female-pattern loss, with too few grafts for coverage. Additional follicles could make restoration possible for them if the follicles keep replacing the hairs they shed.

completion.title: FDA licenses a product that generates new, cycling scalp follicles for androgenetic alopecia.
completion.criterion: FDA approves a biologics license application for a cell-derived product indicated to generate new scalp follicles in people with androgenetic alopecia. Clinical evidence supporting the indication establishes that the new follicles produce terminal hairs and resume growth after regression and rest. FDA examines the product, inspects the listed manufacturing establishments and determines that the product and establishments meet applicable requirements for continued safety, purity and potency.
completion.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 601.2(a), 601.2(d) and 601.20; general biologics licensing requirements.
completion.threshold_quote: only after inspection of the establishment(s) listed in the biologics license application
completion.basis: FDA supplies the licensing decision; RIKEN supplies the requirement to reproduce the hair cycle. The indication specified here applies those published tests to new scalp follicles. The regulations contain no follicle-specific density or durability cutoff. FDA's published list of licensed cellular and gene therapy products contains no regenerated-follicle product.

milestones.title: Reconstructed human follicles produce hair shafts in animal grafts.
milestones.criterion: After transplantation into an animal, a graft contains a newly formed human follicle that produces a differentiated hair shaft. Microscopy documents the shaft and follicular anatomy, and species-specific evidence identifies the follicle as human.
milestones.set_by: The field's hair-reconstitution assay, used by Toyoshima et al. and Lee et al.; the quoted demonstration concerns pluripotent-cell-derived skin.
milestones.threshold_quote: skin organoids form planar hair-bearing skin when grafted onto nude mice.

milestones.title: Regenerated human follicles repeat hair growth cycles in animal grafts.
milestones.criterion: Serial observations after animal engraftment establish that the same newly generated human follicle grows a shaft, regresses and begins growing a new shaft. RIKEN specifies recurrence of growth without prescribing a cycle count or observation period.
milestones.set_by: RIKEN, Regenerating hair in the lab, 2021; its functional criterion concerns mammalian hair, while its reported experiments used mouse cells.
milestones.threshold_quote: a successful hair-regeneration treatment must replicate this cycle.

milestones.title: A regenerated-follicle product demonstrates preclinical safety and efficacy.
milestones.criterion: Before an early human investigation, preclinical studies in relevant models demonstrate the candidate follicle product’s safety and efficacy. They assess the risk of tumour formation, where the administered cells travel and persist, and whether the magnitude and duration of the intended therapeutic effect support clinical testing.
milestones.set_by: International Society for Stem Cell Research, Guidelines for Stem Cell Research and Clinical Translation, recommendations 3.3.1.2, 3.3.2.2, 3.3.2.3 and 3.3.3.1.
milestones.threshold_quote: Early phase human studies should be preceded by a rigorous demonstration of safety and efficacy in preclinical studies.

milestones.title: A regenerated-follicle product is first administered to people under an effective IND.
milestones.criterion: An assembled follicle or follicle-germ product generated from expanded cells is administered to people with androgenetic alopecia in a phase 1 investigation under an IND that is in effect. IND means investigational new drug application. The investigation begins assessment of human safety and treatment delivery. This stage applies to either cell source.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.21(a) and 312.40.
milestones.threshold_quote: the initial introduction of an investigational new drug into humans.

milestones.title: Controlled studies show preliminary efficacy of a regenerated-follicle product in androgenetic alopecia.
milestones.criterion: Controlled phase 2 studies of a regenerated-follicle product in people with androgenetic alopecia obtain preliminary evidence of effectiveness and determine common short-term adverse effects and risks. The claimed indication is formation of new follicles. FDA identifies preliminary evidence of effectiveness as the condition preceding phase 3; it does not prescribe a follicle-specific numerical response threshold.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.21(b) and 312.21(c).

milestones.title: Expanded studies support physician labeling for a regenerated-follicle product.
milestones.criterion: Expanded phase 3 studies of a regenerated-follicle product obtain the additional effectiveness and safety information needed to evaluate its overall benefit–risk relationship and provide an adequate basis for physician labeling for androgenetic alopecia. This is the clinical evidence stage before the licensing decision; manufacturing and establishment requirements remain part of that decision.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.21(c).
milestones.threshold_quote: to provide an adequate basis for physician labeling.

milestones.title: Human cells form new follicles that produce visible hair shafts in culture.
milestones.criterion: Microscopy of a cultured construct made from human cells shows a newly formed follicle with a hair shaft before animal engraftment. The shaft can grow into the interior of a skin organoid or emerge from the surface of a skin construct.
milestones.set_by: The in vitro follicle-formation assay used in engineered human skin by Abaci and colleagues and in human skin organoids by Lee and colleagues.
milestones.threshold_quote: skin organoid hair follicles with visible hair shafts

milestones.title: FDA accepts a biologics license application for a regenerated-follicle product for filing.
milestones.criterion: FDA accepts for filing an application to license the product for generating new scalp follicles in people with androgenetic alopecia. FDA has received the pertinent clinical and nonclinical data, manufacturing information and proposed labeling required for the application.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 601.2(a).
milestones.threshold_quote: shall not be considered as filed until all pertinent information and data have been received by the Food and Drug Administration.

not_found: No follicle-specific FDA, PMDA or ISHRS criterion specifying a minimum new terminal-hair density, repeat-cycle count or follow-up duration was located.
Indexed ClinicalTrials.gov searches identified no registered protocol for transplantation of bioengineered human follicle germs; the registry search page could not be opened.
No published human results establishing repeat cycling of newly generated follicles after transplantation for androgenetic alopecia were located.
No dermatology or hair-restoration society statement was located that judges de novo follicle regeneration for pattern hair loss infeasible or unworthy of pursuit.

results.finding: Adult dermal papilla cell constructs (Fig. 2, n = 9) produced protruding hair shafts in approximately one in three constructs in culture.
results.detail: Figure 2 gives the replicate count for the culture experiment. The text gives an approximate frequency for shaft protrusion and does not give a separate exact tally.

results.finding: Adult dermal papilla cell grafts produced shaft-bearing human follicles in 4 of 7 viable nude-mouse grafts (10 mice per arm).
results.detail: Engineered shafts were intermediate in thickness between the paper’s human terminal and vellus hair comparators.
results.quote: Grafts from four out of these seven mice successfully generated human HFs, whereas none of the seven mice in the FB control experiment induced hair formation.

results.finding: A reconstructed human scalp follicle from one patient with androgenetic alopecia produced a pigmented shaft within 21 days in a nude mouse graft.
results.detail: The Results describe the illustrated graft from one patient. The Methods list two scalp donors overall and give no total graft count for the human experiment.
results.quote: grew a pigmented hair shaft in the transplantation area within 21 days after intracutaneous transplantation into the back skin of nude mice

results.finding: Bioengineered adult mouse vibrissa follicles (n=8 in the serial-observation series) repeated the hair cycle at least 3 times.
results.detail: Figure 5 follows individually identified mouse vibrissae. The paper gives no corresponding serial observations for a regenerated human follicle.
results.quote: The bioengineered pelage and vibrissa follicles repeated the hair cycle at least 3 times during the 80-day period

results.finding: Two imaged WA25 human stem cell-derived follicles had visible hair shafts at day 115 in culture.
results.detail: The shafts grew inward toward the center of the organoid.

results.finding: Outward hair growth occurred in 55% of 27 WA25 human skin organoid xenografts in nude mice.
results.detail: The organoids already contained newly formed follicles at implantation. The grafted follicles resembled second-trimester fetal follicles.
results.quote: Remarkably, we observed 2–5 mm hairs growing out from 55% of the xenografts (15 of 27 xenografts, 3 experiments;

results.finding: Adult human scalp dermal papilla cells combined with neonatal human keratinocytes yielded new follicles in 19 of 37 mouse grafts, with hair shafts documented by histology.
results.detail: The 19 of 37 count is summed from Table 1 and measures grafts containing follicles. Shaft production is documented in representative sections.
results.quote: Epithelial compartments of the HFs were intact with concentric layers of inner and outer root sheaths, sebaceous glands and hair shaft
